title: Employee Onboarding Videos From Your Existing PowerPoint (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: Onboarding Videos From Your Existing PowerPoint
bullets: Turn repeated sessions into video
Watch on day one, at their own pace
The same accurate message every time
slides.notes: Your team presents the same onboarding deck to every new starter. What if they could watch it on day one, at their own pace, with the same message every time?

slides.title: Audit your decks into three groups
bullets: Stable and standard: ideal for video
Changes often: keep out or on one slide
Needs a human: keep live
slides.notes: Start by sorting your decks. Stable policies and company history suit video, things that change often stay out, and welcomes and Q&A stay live.

slides.title: Short videos beat one long one
bullets: Five six-minute videos, not one thirty-minute video
Welcome and how we work
Policies you need to know
Systems and tools
slides.notes: A new hire is more likely to finish five six-minute videos than one thirty-minute video. So split your content into short, focused topics.

slides.title: Clean up slides before converting
bullets: One idea per slide
"You can work from home up to three days a week"
24pt or larger body text
Roles, not names: "your manager"
slides.notes: Tidy each deck first. Give every slide one idea and a headline that makes a point, and swap stale names for roles like your manager.

slides.title: Speaker notes become the voiceover
bullets: Write as you'd explain to a new colleague
Keep sentences short
Spell out acronyms the first time
Respell names the voice mispronounces
slides.notes: Your speaker notes become the voiceover, so write them like you're explaining things to a new colleague. Keep sentences short and spell out acronyms.

slides.title: Update the slide, not the recording
bullets: Edit the slide and its notes
Convert again and replace the MP4
Review every six months, with an owner
Pro: a.i.-directed videos
slides.notes: When a policy changes, just edit and convert again. On Pro, a.i. directs each video so it lands like a produced welcome. Try Basic first at powerpoint2vid.com.
